structure.title: A summer opening
structure.text: Grand Isle creates room for new sensations and attachments outside Edna's ordinary household routine.

structure.title: Returning to daily life
structure.text: Back in New Orleans, new desires encounter the arrangements of marriage, money, motherhood, and social expectation.

people.name: Edna Pontellier
people.text: A young wife and mother from Kentucky, married into New Orleans Creole society, who begins one summer to feel that her life is not quite her own.

people.name: Robert Lebrun
people.text: The charming son of the family who keep the summer resort, who devotes himself every season to a married woman and pays attention to Edna.

people.name: Adèle Ratignolle
people.text: Edna's friend at the resort, a devoted and beautiful mother who seems entirely at home in her role as wife and mother.

context.title: A social role
context.text: Edna's comfort comes within expectations about a wife's availability and conduct. Wanting something different affects arrangements other people regard as settled.

context.title: Music and sensation
context.text: Art and physical experience give Edna feelings she cannot initially explain. Understanding follows sensation unevenly.
context.takeaway: Awakening is not the same as a settled plan.

notice.why: Bodily freedom carries both pleasure and uncertainty.
Different lives prevent one model of womanhood from explaining everyone.

opening: Edna Pontellier has a husband, children, and a comfortable place in New Orleans society. During a summer by the sea, she begins wanting things that cannot be fitted neatly around them. Swimming, music, and another man's attention make her feel that a life she had accepted might be only one possibility. Kate Chopin follows the discovery into ordinary arrangements about houses, money, and duty, where a woman's desire for a life of her own becomes everyone else's problem to explain away.
